speaker: Sheldon
text: Here's the problem with teleportation.

speaker: Leonard
text: Lay it on me.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Assuming a device could be invented... Which would identify the state of matter of an individual in one location... And transmit that to a distant location for reassembly... You wouldn't have transported the individual... You would have destroyed him in one location and re-created him in another.

speaker: Leonard
text: How about that.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I would never use a transporter. The original Sheldon would have to be disintegrated... In order to create a new Sheldon.

speaker: Leonard
text: Would the new Sheldon be in any way an improvement on the old Sheldon?

speaker: Sheldon
text: No, he would be exactly the same.

speaker: Leonard
text: That is a problem.

speaker: Sheldon
text: So you see it too?

speaker: ENSEMBLE
text: Dr. Hofstadter, Dr. Cooper.

speaker: unknown
text: Dr. Gablehauser.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Gentlemen, I'd like you to meet Dennis Kim. Dennis is a highly sought-after doctoral candidate. We're hoping to have him do graduate work here. - Graduate work, very impressive. - And he's only 15 years old.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Not bad. I myself started graduate school at 14.

speaker: Dennis
text: Well, I lost a year while my family was tunneling out of North Korea.

speaker: Leonard
text: Advantage, Kim.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: I thought maybe you could show Dennis around. Let him see why we're the best physics research facility in the country.

speaker: Dennis
text: I know you're not. You don't have an open science grid computer or a free electron laser. The string theory research being done is a dead end.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Excuse me, that is my research, and it is by no means a dead end.

speaker: Dennis
text: Well, obviously, you don't see it yet, but trust me, you will.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Dennis, we've discussed this. We're in the process of updating our equipment. We welcome your input on our research goals. We agree to look the other way if you use 20 percent... Of the money you attract to smuggle your grandfather out of Pyongyang.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: We want him here, boys. - Make it happen. - Yes, sir.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You can count on us. We're on it. What the hell do you mean, "dead end"?

speaker: Dennis
text: I mean, the whole landscape of false vacuums in string theory... Could be as large as 10 to the 500th power. In addition... Ooh, look, chocolate milk.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I sense a disturbance in the force.

speaker: unknown
text: A bad feeling I have about this. Mm.

speaker: Leonard
text: So how long have you been in america?

speaker: Dennis
text: - A year and a half. - No kidding.

speaker: Leonard
text: - You speak English really well. - So do you.

speaker: Dennis
text: Except for your tendency to end sentences with prepositions.

speaker: Leonard
text: What are you talking about?

speaker: Sheldon
text: He's not wrong. All right, and this is my office.

speaker: Dennis
text: - Is this part of the tour? - Nope. Goodbye.

speaker: Leonard
text: Sheldon, we've hardly shown him anything.

speaker: Sheldon
text: All right, this is my desk. These are my books. This is my door. Please close it behind you, goodbye.

speaker: Dennis
text: You're doing work in quantum loop corrections. - Keen observation, goodbye. - You see where you went wrong, don't you?

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Leonard. - Ha. - Yeah? - Get him out.

speaker: Leonard
text: Come, I'll show you the rec center. They've got nautilus equipment.

speaker: Dennis
text: Do I look like I lift weights?

speaker: Leonard
text: Not heavy ones.

speaker: Dennis
text: It's startling you haven't considered a lorentz invariant or field theory approach.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You think I haven't considered it? - You really think I haven't considered it? - Have you considered it?

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Get him out, Leonard. - Come on, Dennis.

speaker: Leonard
text: I'll show you the radiation lab.

speaker: Dennis
text: Wow. You won the Stevenson award?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes. In fact, I am the youngest person ever to win it.

speaker: Dennis
text: Really? How old?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Fourteen and a half.

speaker: Dennis
text: Mm. You were the youngest ever to win it.

speaker: Leonard
text: It's like looking into an obnoxious mirror, isn't it?

speaker: unknown
text: Mm. This is really delicious, isn't it?

speaker: unknown
text: Still can't talk to me unless you're drunk, huh? Oh, sweetie, you are so damaged.

speaker: Howard
text: Hey, I'm damaged too. How about a hug for Howie?

speaker: Penny
text: Sure. Raj, hug Howard.

speaker: Leonard
text: Something you'd like to share? A tale of woe perhaps?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Fifteen years old. Dennis Kim is 15 years old and he's already correcting my work. Today, I went from being Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart to... You know, that other guy.

speaker: Howard
text: Antonio salieri?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, god, now even you're smarter than me.

speaker: Howard
text: You know, you don't have so many friends that you can afford to start insulting them.

speaker: Leonard
text: Just eat, Sheldon. You'll feel better.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Why waste food? When a cow goes dry, they don't keep feeding it... They just take her out and shoot her between the eyes.

speaker: Penny
text: I'm confused. Did Sheldon stop giving milk?

speaker: Leonard
text: You can't let this kid get to you. You knew that someday, someone would come along who's younger and smarter.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, but I assumed I would've been dead hundreds of years. And that there'd be an asterisk by his name because he'd be a cyborg.

speaker: Penny
text: So you got a little competition. I really don't see what the big deal is.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Of course you don't. You've never excelled at anything.

speaker: Penny
text: I don't understand, exactly how did he get any friends in the first place?

speaker: Leonard
text: What are you gonna do, just give up?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Yes, it's what a rational person does when his entire life's work is invalidated... By a postpubescent Asian wunderkind. He ceases his fruitless efforts, he donates his body to scientific research... And he waits to die.

speaker: Penny
text: I'm confused again. Is he waiting, or do we get to shoot him between the eyes?

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Hey. - Hey. I've decided you're right. - My career is not over. - Great. But since Dennis Kim has rendered my research pointless... I just have to find something else to focus on.

speaker: Sheldon
text: So I've decided I'm going to collaborate with you.

speaker: Sheldon
text: So, what exactly is it you do? I know you chatter on about it all the time, but I've never really paid attention.

speaker: Leonard
text: Right now, I'm designing an experiment to study the soft component... Of cosmic radiation at sea level, but I don't need help.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, sure you do. Now see, what's this here in the schematic, a laser array?

speaker: Leonard
text: - Yes. - Now, hmm...

speaker: Sheldon
text: What happens if you use argon lasers instead of helium-neon?

speaker: Leonard
text: - It would blow up. - Are you sure?

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Pretty sure. - "Pretty sure" is not very scientific. Is this how you normally work? Just hunches and guesses and stuff?

speaker: Leonard
text: Okay. I understand that you're going through a bit of a career crisis. You're searching for some other area where you can feel valuable and productive. But I need to tell you something, and listen carefully. - All right. - Go away.

speaker: Sheldon
text: If you're concerned about sharing credit with me, your name can go first... I'm going.

speaker: unknown
text: It's a small brown paper bag, ma. I'm looking at it right now. Why would I make that up? There's no ding dong in it.

speaker: unknown
text: How are two ding dongs tomorrow gonna help me today? So this is engineering, huh? I'll talk to you later.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Engineering, where the noble semiskilled laborers... Execute the vision of those who think and dream. Hello, oompa loompas of science.

speaker: Howard
text: Sheldon, what are you doing here?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I just came by to say hello.

speaker: Howard
text: For three years, you've never come by to say hello.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Well, up until now, I've had better things to do. So, what are we making today?

speaker: Howard
text: A small payload support structure for a European science experimental package... - That's going up on the next space shuttle. - Really? How does it work? It will be attached to the payload bay... And the sensor apparatus will rest on it.

speaker: Sheldon
text: So it's a shelf.

speaker: Howard
text: No, you don't understand. During acceleration, it needs to stay perfectly level and provide... Yeah, okay, it's a shelf.

speaker: Sheldon
text: I notice you're using titanium. Did you give any consideration to carbon nanotubes? They're lighter, cheaper and have twice the tensile strength.

speaker: Howard
text: Sheldon, there's a diploma in my office that says I have a master's in engineering.

speaker: Sheldon
text: And you also have a note from your mother that says, "I love you, bubula."

speaker: Sheldon
text: But neither of those is a cogent argument for titanium over nanotubes.

speaker: Howard
text: - Sheldon. - Yes? Go away.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Did Leonard tell you to say that?

speaker: Howard
text: No, I thought of it all by myself.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Huh? Can't be a coincidence. There must be some causal link I'm missing.

speaker: Raj
text: Go away.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Curiouser and curiouser.

speaker: Leonard
text: - Is he here? - If he were, I wouldn't be.

speaker: Raj
text: You know what he did? He watched me work... And then started to design a simple piece of software that could replace me.

speaker: Leonard
text: Is that even possible?

speaker: Raj
text: As it turns out, yes.

speaker: Howard
text: - Something's gotta be done about him. - Like what?

speaker: Leonard
text: He'll never cope with the fact that some 15-year-old is smarter... And more accomplished than he is.

speaker: Raj
text: What if something were to happen to him so he was no longer a threat to Sheldon?

speaker: Howard
text: Then our problem would be solved.

speaker: Leonard
text: Hang on, are we talking about murdering Dennis Kim? I'm not saying no.

speaker: Howard
text: We don't have to go that far. There are other means.

speaker: Raj
text: We can't send him back to North Korea. He knows how to get out.

speaker: Howard
text: The only thing we need to do is make this Kim kid lose his focus.

speaker: Leonard
text: It won't happen. He is not interested in anything but physics.

speaker: Howard
text: - What about biology? - What? You know, biology. The one thing that can completely derail a world-class mind.

speaker: Leonard
text: - Howard, he's 15. - Yeah, so?

speaker: Howard
text: When I was 15, I met Denise palmeri... And my grade point average fell from a 5.0 to a 1.8.

speaker: Raj
text: She was sleeping with you?

speaker: Howard
text: No, I just wasted a lot of time thinking about what it would be like if she did.

speaker: unknown
text: Oh, good, you're all here. I've decided that if the three of you drop whatever you're working on and join me... We could lick cold fusion in less than a decade, 12 years tops.

speaker: unknown
text: Go away?

speaker: unknown
text: Could it be me?

speaker: unknown
text: Hey, guys, what's up?

speaker: Howard
text: We need a hot 15-year-old Asian girl with a thing for smart guys.

speaker: Leonard
text: - What? - Howard, that's racist. Any 15-year-old girl will do the trick.

speaker: Raj
text: It's possible she may have misunderstood us.

speaker: Sheldon
text: - Dr. Cooper. Oh, are we interrupting? - No, no, please come in. I think you'll appreciate this. This is very exciting.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: - What are you working on? - Something remarkable.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Since my prospects for the nobel prize in physics have disappeared... thank you. I've decided to refocus my efforts and use my people skills... To win the nobel peace prize. Look, I'm going to solve the middle east crisis... By building an exact replica of Jerusalem in the middle of the Mexican desert.

speaker: Sheldon
text: You know, it's like the baseball movie. "Build it and they will come."

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Who will come?

speaker: Sheldon
text: The Jewish people.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: What if they don't come?

speaker: Sheldon
text: We'll make it nice, put out a spread.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Okay, well, speaking of spreads... We're having a welcoming party this afternoon for Mr. Kim... - Who's agreed to join us at the university. - Of course he has.

speaker: Sheldon
text: The oracle told us little Neo was the one. You can see the matrix, can't you?

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Okay, well, obviously, you're very busy with your, ah, um... Come, Dennis.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: You'll have to excuse Dr. Cooper. He's been under a lot of, um... He's nuts.

speaker: Sheldon
text: They'll come, they'll settle and I'll win the prize

speaker: Sheldon
text: I don't understand your objections, professor goldfarb. Why wouldn't the sonora desert make a perfectly good promised land?

speaker: Goldfarb
text: Go away.

speaker: Sheldon
text: We could call it nuevo Jerusalem.

speaker: Goldfarb
text: Please go away.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Said pharaoh to Moses.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Why are all these young women here?

speaker: Leonard
text: It's take your daughter to work day.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Really? I was not aware of that.

speaker: Raj
text: Oh, yes. There was a very official e-mail... That was sent to everyone whose files indicated... They had daughters between the ages of 14 and 16.

speaker: Raj
text: - Smooth. - Thank you.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: There's the man of the hour.

speaker: Leonard
text: So we have a socially awkward genius in a room of attractive age-appropriate women.

speaker: Howard
text: All he has to do is hook up with one.

speaker: Leonard
text: Anyone else see the flaw in this plan?

speaker: Raj
text: We need a social catalyst.

speaker: Leonard
text: Like what? We can't get 15-year-old girls drunk. - Or can we? - No, we can't.

speaker: Howard
text: I don't think you mean we can't. I think you mean we shouldn't.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Hey, Howard, you're a Jew. If there was another wailing wall exactly like the one in Jerusalem... But close to taco stands and cheap prescription drugs... Would you still wail at it?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Okay, it's definitely me.

speaker: Leonard
text: We cannot leave this to chance. Let's pick a girl... And figure out how to get her with Dennis.

speaker: Raj
text: How about that one?

speaker: Howard
text: Uh-uh. I know the type. Cheerleader, student council, goes out with jocks. Won't look at anybody in the gifted program. If she does agree to go out, it turns out to be a setup. You're in your mom's car with your pants off while the whole football team laughs.

speaker: Howard
text: - Are you crying? - No, I have allergies.

speaker: Raj
text: Okay. Uh... Oh, hey, how about her?

speaker: Leonard
text: Sure, if he wants to spend years doing her homework... While she drinks herself into a stupor with nonfat white Russians. And you're holding her head while she's puking... And wishes more guys were like you. She gets into Cornell, because you wrote her essay. And you drive up to visit her one weekend and she acts like she doesn't know you.

speaker: Raj
text: Okay, so not her either.

speaker: Raj
text: How about her?

speaker: Howard
text: Interesting, kind of pretty, a little chubby, so probably low self-esteem.

speaker: Leonard
text: I think that's our girl. One of us should go talk to her.

speaker: Raj
text: I can't talk to her, you do it.

speaker: Leonard
text: I can't just go up and talk to her. Howard, you talk to her.

speaker: Howard
text: I don't know, she'll never go for the kid once she gets a peek at this.

speaker: Raj
text: In India, this would be simpler. Five minutes with her dad, 20 goats and a laptop, and we'd be done.

speaker: Leonard
text: Well, we're not in India.

speaker: Raj
text: Why don't we do it your way, then? We'll arrange for her to move in across the hall so he can pathetically moon over her.

speaker: Leonard
text: - Okay, that was uncalled for. - You started it, dude.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Could I have everyone's attention, please? What a wonderful occasion this is. And how fortunate that it should fall on take your daughter to work day. We're here to welcome Mr. Dennis Kim to our little family.

speaker: unknown
text: Welcome, Dennis Kim.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Mr. Kim was not only the valedictorian at Stanford university... He is also the youngest recipient of the prestigious Stevenson award.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Youngest till the cyborgs rise up.

speaker: Gablehouser
text: And now, without any further ado... Let me introduce the man of the hour, Mr. Dennis Kim. Dennis? Dennis.

speaker: Dennis
text: What?

speaker: Gablehouser
text: Would you like to tell us about your upcoming research?

speaker: Dennis
text: Oh, no, thanks. I'm going to the mall with Emma.

speaker: Leonard
text: The kid got a girl.

speaker: Raj
text: Unbelievable.

speaker: Howard
text: Did anyone see how he did it?

speaker: unknown
text: Don't worry, I've got this. Ladies and gentlemen, honored daughters... While Mr. Kim, by virtue of his youth and naiveté... Has fallen prey to the inexplicable need for human contact... Let me step in and assure you that my research will go on uninterrupted. And that social relationships will continue to baffle and repulse me. Thank you.

speaker: Howard
text: - He's back. - Yeah, mission accomplished.

speaker: Raj
text: Forget the mission. How did that little yutz get a girl on his own?

speaker: Howard
text: I guess times have changed since we were young. Smart is the new sexy.

speaker: Leonard
text: Then why do we go home alone every night? We're still smart.

speaker: Raj
text: Maybe we're too smart. So smart, it's off-putting.

speaker: Howard
text: Yeah, let's go with that.

speaker: Howard
text: Unbelievable. Components I built are on the space station... And I get a ticket for launching a rocket in the park.

speaker: Leonard
text: I don't know if the ticket was so much for the launch as for telling the policewoman: "You have to frisk me. I have another rocket in my pants."

speaker: Raj
text: Hey, look at that. It's Dennis Kim.

speaker: Howard
text: Wow, I almost didn't recognize him.

speaker: Raj
text: I kind of feel bad about what we did to him.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah, we really ruined his life.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Screw him, he was weak.
